G1 (THE DECIDING LEG, and it needs no baseline): p90(mode 2) is within 2 of p90(mode 1), worst run against worst run. FAILS IF mode 2's p90 exceeds mode 1's by more than 2 -- which is the world in which mode 2 IS cheaper on a real title and the recommendation flips to shipping mode 2. G3 (THE BAIL RATE -- the leg that makes G1 interpretable). Mode 2 skips the hold only on FSK_SEG_NO_DRAW; a scan hitting FIFO_SKEW_SCAN_MAX_WORDS falls through to mode 1's path. So 'mode 2 costs what mode 1 costs' is equally consistent with the mechanism working on draw-dense content and with the pre-scan bailing every time, and those call for opposite decisions. held(n)/kicks reads as an intact guarantee under both. The discriminator is already on the `fifoskew` line: big / scan n < 0.01 in both mode-2 runs. FAILS IF the scan is bailing.

G4 (AN INTERNAL CONTROL, an identity that must hold by construction): scan draw + nodraw + wrap + big == scan n, summed over every window of every mode-2 run. A violation indicts the instrument.

G5 (THE PRIOR, STATED SO IT CAN FAIL): nodraw / scan n < 0.20 on Galleon in both mode-2 runs -- i.e. Galleon's submissions mostly DO carry a draw, so there is little for a selective bound to skip. The transfer this leg refuses to make is disc -> title. FAILS IF Galleon turns out to be draw-sparse on this device, in which case G1's reading changes completely.
